summary: Michael W. Charney is a historian who earned his PhD from the University of Michigan in 1999. In 2001, he was appointed Professor of Asian and Military History at SOAS University of London.

Michael W. Meister is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his BA, MA, and PhD from Harvard University, also studying at the University of Pennsylvania, where he became a professor around 1976.

Michael Weiers was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist who completed his doctorate at the University of Bonn. He served as a professor at the University of Bonn (1972–2003) and as an honorary professor at Inner Mongolia University.

Michael Wenger is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at The New School and with Mel Weitsman. He served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at the San Francisco Zen Center and founded the Dragons Leap Meditation Center.

Michael Willis is an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Victoria and University of Chicago. He was a curator at the British Museum (1994–2014) and later served as Principal Investigator for projects at the ERC and British Library.

Michael Witzel is a linguist and Indologist who studied under scholars including Karl Hoffmann and Paul Thieme. He led the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project, held the Chair of Sanskrit at Leiden University, and later served as professor at Harvard University.
Michael Yorke is a religious studies scholar who studied as a graduate student at Yale University (attested 2026) and held a post there.

Michael Zimmermann is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg. He held a professorship at Stanford University in 2003 and became a professor and director at the University of Hamburg around 2007.

Michael von Brück is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied at the University of Rostock and University of Madras. He held professorships at the University of Regensburg (1988–1991) and the University of Munich (c. 1991–2014).
Michaela Haas is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Bonn under Peter Schwieger, also studying under Rechungpa and Jigme Namgyal Dzigar Kongtrul.

Michaela Mross is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed her PhD at the University of Munich. She held a postdoctoral fellowship at UC Berkeley and became an assistant professor at Stanford University in 2016.

Michaël Peyrot is a linguist, Indologist, and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Leiden University. He held academic posts at Leiden University and worked at the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (2014–2016).

Michel Bitbol is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Paris Diderot University. He held positions at the CNRS, the University of Paris, Linacre College, Oxford, and the École Normale Supérieure.

Michel Bréal was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber in Berlin. He served as a professor at the Collège de France and as director at the EPHE.

Michel Clasquin-Johnson is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed his degrees, including his doctoral thesis, at the University of South Africa, where he held an academic post in 1990.
Michel Hulin was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the École Normale Supérieure, under Olivier Lacombe, and at Paris-Sorbonne University, where he later held a post from 1981 to 1998.
Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Jean Boisselier and served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University.

Michel Ledrus was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He held academic posts at KU Leuven in 1931 and the Pontifical Gregorian University (1932–1933), later serving as spiritual director at Collegio Bellarmino in 1949.

Michel Lejeune was a linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the University of Poitiers, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the University of Paris.

Michel Mohr is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology who completed his PhD at the University of Geneva and studied under Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at Hanazono University and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.
